sections.heading: SNAPPING
sections.content:
ProBuilder provides a dedicated geometric snapping subsystem implemented across `ProBuilderSnapping` (runtime math) and `EditorSnapping` (editor settings and tool orchestration). Snapping operates in scalar, 3D vector, per-vertex, and ray-constrained modes.

1. Scalar and Vector Snapping Algorithms:
- `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(float val, float snap)`: Evaluates whether `snap == 0`. If zero, returns `val` unmodified. Otherwise, computes `snap * Mathf.Round(val / snap)`, quantizing the value to the nearest integer multiple of `snap`.
- `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(Vector3 val, Vector3 snap)`: Quantizes each coordinate independently. Evaluates whether `Mathf.Abs(snap.x) > 0.0001f` (using a minimum epsilon threshold to ignore floating-point noise). If true, calculates `Snap(val.x, snap.x)`; otherwise leaves `val.x` unmodified. The same check applies to `val.y` and `val.z`.
- `ProBuilderSnapping.SnapVertices(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> indexes, Vector3 snap)`: Snaps mesh vertices in world space. For every index in `indexes`, retrieves the local vertex position from `mesh.positionsInternal`, transforms it to world space via `mesh.transform.TransformPoint`, applies `Snap(worldPoint, snap)`, and converts the result back to local space using `mesh.transform.InverseTransformPoint`.
- `ProBuilderSnapping.GetSnappingMaskBasedOnNormalVector(Vector3 normal)`: Generates a vector mask based on face orientation. For each axis (X, Y, Z), if `Mathf.Approximately(Mathf.Abs(normal[axis]), 1f)`, the mask component is set to `0f`; otherwise `1f`. This prevents snapping along the normal direction of an aligned surface while permitting snapping across the plane of the face.
- `ProBuilderSnapping.IsCardinalDirection(Vector3 direction)`: Returns true if exactly one component is non-zero (`Mathf.Abs(direction[axis]) > 0f`) and the remaining two components are approximately zero (`Mathf.Approximately(direction[other], 0f)`).

2. Ray Snapping Algorithm (`SnapValueOnRay`):
- `ProBuilderSnapping.SnapValueOnRay(Ray ray, float distance, float snap, Vector3Mask mask)`: Determines the closest discrete grid snap point along a movement ray.
  a. Initializes `nearest = k_MaxRaySnapDistance` (`Mathf.Infinity`).
  b. Constructs `forwardRay = new Ray(ray.origin, ray.direction)` and `backwardsRay = new Ray(ray.origin, -ray.direction)`.
  c. Iterates through the 3 primary axes (i = 0, 1, 2). If `mask[i] > 0f`:
     - Creates axis mask `dir = new Vector3Mask((byte)(1 << i))`.
     - Projects the movement ray vector `ray.direction * Math.MakeNonZero(distance)` onto `dir * Mathf.Sign(ray.direction[i])` using `Vector3.Project`.
     - Computes projected point `pnt = ray.origin + prj` and creates a snapping plane: `plane = new Plane(dir, Snap(pnt, dir * snap))`.
     - If `Mathf.Abs(plane.GetDistanceToPoint(ray.origin)) < 0.0001f`, sets `nearest = 0f` and continues.
     - Raycasts `forwardRay` against `plane`; if intersection distance `d` satisfies `Mathf.Abs(d) < Mathf.Abs(nearest)`, updates `nearest = d`.
     - Raycasts `backwardsRay` against `plane`; if intersection distance `d` satisfies `Mathf.Abs(d) < Mathf.Abs(nearest)`, updates `nearest = -d`.
  d. Returns the snapped 3D position `ray.origin + ray.direction * (Mathf.Abs(nearest) >= k_MaxRaySnapDistance ? distance : nearest)`.

3. ProGrids Integration and Snap Modes:
- ProGrids integration operates through `ProGridsInterface`, a reflection bridge that probes for types `UnityEditor.ProGrids.ProGridsEditor`, `ProGrids.Editor.ProGridsEditor`, `ProGrids.Editor.pg_Editor`, `ProGrids.pg_Editor`, and `pg_Editor`.
- Delegates bind to ProGrids methods: `s_ProGridsActiveDelegate`, `s_SnapEnabledDelegate`, `s_ProGridsSnapAsGroupDelegate`, `s_IsFullGridEnabledDelegate`, `s_GetActiveGridOffsetDelegate`, `s_SnapValueDelegate`, and `s_GetPivotDelegate`.
- `ProBuilderEditor.PushToGrid(float snapVal)` subscribes to `ProGridsInterface.SubscribePushToGridEvent`. When triggered, it queries coincident vertices via `mesh.GetCoincidentVertices(mesh.selectedIndexesInternal)`, invokes `ProBuilderSnapping.SnapVertices(mesh, indexes, Vector3.one * snapVal)`, and calls `mesh.ToMesh()` followed by `mesh.Refresh()`.
- `EditorSnapping.snapMode` resolves to:
  - `SnapMode.Relative`: Active when `EditorSnapSettings.incrementalSnapActive` is enabled. Snapping increments are relative to the drag start.
  - `SnapMode.World`: Active when `ProGridsInterface.SnapEnabled()` is true or when `EditorSnapSettings.gridSnapActive` is true and `Tools.pivotRotation == PivotRotation.Global`. Snaps directly to absolute world grid coordinates.
  - `SnapMode.None`: Snapping is inactive.

4. Element Snapping During Movement:
- In `ProbuilderMoveTool` and `VertexManipulationTool`, element translation respects `EditorSnapping.snapAsGroup` (backed by user preference `ProBuilder.SnapSettings.s_SnapAsGroup`, default `true`, or ProGrids `GetSnapAsGroup()`):
  - Group Snapping (`m_SnapAsGroup == true`): The tool calculates the global handle position, snaps the handle pivot to the grid via `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap` or `ProBuilderSnapping.SnapValueOnRay`, and applies the resulting delta uniformly to all selected vertices/faces/edges. This preserves relative offsets between elements.
  - Individual Snapping (`m_SnapAsGroup == false`): When `EditorSnapping.snapMode == SnapMode.World`, each vertex is transformed to world space (`wp`), snapped individually to the grid via `ProBuilderSnapping.Snap(wp, snapValue)` (or along constrained single axes with `SnapValueOnRay`), and converted back to model space using `worldToLocal.MultiplyPoint3x4(snap)`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, scalar and vector snapping can be implemented using `Mathf.snapped()` or `Vector3.snapped(step)`. World-space vertex snapping is performed by transforming vertex arrays with `Node3D.global_transform`, calling `.snapped(snap_step)`, and converting back via `global_transform.affine_inverse()`. Group vs individual snapping modes in Godot editor gizmos correspond to snapping the gizmo transform origin vs snapping individual vertex coordinates.

sections.heading: MATH
sections.content:
The `Math` static class defines the foundational geometric and linear algebra functions utilized throughout mesh generation, editing, UV manipulation, and spatial queries.

1. Constants and Tolerances:
- `phi`: The golden ratio constant `1.618033988749895f`.
- `k_FltEpsilon`: Machine epsilon `float.Epsilon`.
- `k_FltCompareEpsilon`: Vertex comparison tolerance `0.0001f`.
- `handleEpsilon`: Minimum handle movement threshold `0.0001f`.

2. Geometric Point Generation and Angles:
- `PointInCircumference(float radius, float angleInDegrees, Vector2 origin)`: Converts degrees to radians with `Mathf.Deg2Rad * angleInDegrees`, computing `x = radius * Mathf.Cos(rad) + origin.x` and `y = radius * Mathf.Sin(rad) + origin.y`.
- `PointInEllipseCircumference(float xRadius, float yRadius, float angleInDegrees, Vector2 origin, out Vector2 tangent)`: Computes ellipse perimeter point `x = xRadius * cosA + origin.x`, `y = yRadius * sinA + origin.y`, and normalizes tangent vector `tangent = new Vector2(-y / (yRadius * yRadius), x / (xRadius * xRadius)).normalized`.
- `PointInEllipseCircumferenceWithConstantAngle(float xRadius, float yRadius, float angleInDegrees, Vector2 origin, out Vector2 tangent)`: Calculates constant angular perimeter distribution using `tan = Mathf.Tan(rad)`, `tan2 = tan * tan`, `newX = (xRadius * yRadius) / Mathf.Sqrt(yRadius * yRadius + xRadius * xRadius * tan2)` (negated if `cosA < 0`), and `newY = (xRadius * yRadius) / Mathf.Sqrt(xRadius * xRadius + yRadius * yRadius / tan2)` (negated if `sinA < 0`).
- `PointInSphere(float radius, float latitudeAngle, float longitudeAngle)`: Computes spherical 3D coordinates `x = radius * Cos(lat) * Sin(lon)`, `y = radius * Sin(lat) * Sin(lon)`, `z = radius * Cos(lon)`.
- `SignedAngle(Vector2 a, Vector2 b)`: Calculates `t = Vector2.Angle(a, b)`. If `b.x - a.x < 0`, returns `360f - t`; otherwise returns `t`.

3. Distance, Area, and Centroid Metrics:
- `SqrDistance(Vector3 a, Vector3 b)`: Computes squared distance `dx*dx + dy*dy + dz*dz` without square root evaluation.
- `TriangleArea(Vector3 x, Vector3 y, Vector3 z)`: Implements high-precision triangle area calculation using squared edge lengths `a = SqrDistance(x, y)`, `b = SqrDistance(y, z)`, `c = SqrDistance(z, x)`:
  $$\text{Area} = \sqrt{\frac{2ab + 2bc + 2ca - a^2 - b^2 - c^2}{16}}$$
- `PolygonArea(Vector3[] vertices, int[] indexes)`: Sums `TriangleArea` for every triangle triple `indexes[i]`, `indexes[i+1]`, `indexes[i+2]` in the polygon index buffer.
- `Average(IList<Vector2>/Vector3/Vector4 array, IList<int> indexes = null)`: Computes the arithmetic mean (centroid) across all vectors or subset `indexes`.

4. 2D Transformations, Reflections, and Line Distances:
- `RotateAroundPoint(this Vector2 v, Vector2 origin, float theta)`: Rotates 2D vector around pivot `origin` by angle `theta` in degrees using standard sine/cosine translation matrices.
- `ScaleAroundPoint(this Vector2 v, Vector2 origin, Vector2 scale)`: Scales 2D vector relative to pivot: `(v - origin) * scale + origin`.
- `Perpendicular(Vector2 value)`: Returns 2D orthogonal vector `new Vector2(-value.y, value.x)`.
- `ReflectPoint(Vector2 point, Vector2 lineStart, Vector2 lineEnd)`: Reflects point across a 2D line segment using orthogonal projection and angle distance.
- `SqrDistanceRayPoint(Ray ray, Vector3 point)`: Computes squared distance from 3D point to ray: `Vector3.Cross(ray.direction, point - ray.origin).sqrMagnitude`.
- `DistancePointLineSegment(Vector2/Vector3 point, lineStart, lineEnd)`: Computes minimum distance from a point to a finite segment. Projects point onto segment with parameter `t = Dot(point - lineStart, lineEnd - lineStart) / l2`. If `t < 0.0`, returns distance to `lineStart`; if `t > 1.0`, returns distance to `lineEnd`; otherwise returns distance to `lineStart + t * (lineEnd - lineStart)`.
- `GetNearestPointRayRay(Vector3 ao, Vector3 ad, Vector3 bo, Vector3 bd)`: Finds the closest point on ray A to ray B in 3D skew space using dot products:
  $$c = bo - ao, \quad n = -\text{dot}(ad, bd) \cdot \text{dot}(bd, c) + \text{dot}(ad, c) \cdot \text{dot}(bd, bd)$$
  $$d = \text{dot}(ad, ad) \cdot \text{dot}(bd, bd) - \text{dot}(ad, bd)^2, \quad \text{Result} = ao + ad \cdot (n / d)$$

5. Line Segment, Polygon, and Ray Intersections:
- `GetLineSegmentIntersect(Vector2 p0, Vector2 p1, Vector2 p2, Vector2 p3, ref Vector2 intersect)`: 2D segment intersection solver. Uses parametric cross products `s` and `t`. Returns `true` if `0 <= s <= 1` and `0 <= t <= 1`, setting `intersect = p0 + t * s1`.
- `PointInPolygon(Vector2[] polygon, Vector2 point, int[] indexes = null)`: Ray-casting parity point-in-polygon algorithm. First tests `Bounds2D(polygon, indexes).ContainsPoint(point)`. If contained, casts a horizontal/directional ray from outside the bounds `bounds.center + dir * (bounds.size.y + bounds.size.x + 2f)` to `point`. Counts line segment intersections against all polygon edges; returns `collisions % 2 != 0`.
- `RectIntersectsLineSegment(Rect rect, Vector2/Vector3 a, Vector2/Vector3 b)`: Invokes `Clipping.RectContainsLineSegment(rect, a.x, a.y, b.x, b.y)`. Implements Cohen-Sutherland clipping using `OutCode` bitmask flags (`Inside = 0`, `Left = 1`, `Right = 2`, `Bottom = 4`, `Top = 8`), repeatedly testing immediate bitwise acceptance (`outcode0 | outcode1 == Inside`), immediate bitwise rejection (`(outcode0 & outcode1) != Inside`), and clipping outside points against rectangle boundaries.
- `RayIntersectsTriangle(Ray InRay, Vector3 InTriangleA, Vector3 InTriangleB, Vector3 InTriangleC, out float OutDistance, out Vector3 OutPoint)`: Möller–Trumbore ray-triangle intersection algorithm. Calculates edge vectors `e1 = B - A`, `e2 = C - A`, determinant vector `P = Cross(dir, e2)`, and determinant `det = Dot(e1, P)`. Non-culling branch rejects `det` near zero. Computes distance vector `T = origin - A`, barycentric coordinate `u = Dot(T, P) * inv_det` (rejecting `u < 0` or `u > 1`), vector `Q = Cross(T, e1)`, barycentric coordinate `v = Dot(dir, Q) * inv_det` (rejecting `v < 0` or `u + v > 1`), and ray distance `t = Dot(e2, Q) * inv_det`. If `t > Epsilon`, sets `OutDistance = t` and reconstructs intersection point `OutPoint = u*B + v*C + (1 - u - v)*A`.
- `RayIntersectsTriangle2`: Non-allocating variant of Möller–Trumbore using pre-allocated static scratch vectors `tv1`, `tv2`, `tv3`, `tv4` and outputting `ref float distance` and `ref Vector3 normal`.

6. Normal, Tangent, and Bitangent Calculations:
- `Normal(Vector3 p0, Vector3 p1, Vector3 p2)`: Calculates `Cross(p1 - p0, p2 - p0).normalized`.
- `Normal(IList<Vertex> vertices, IList<int> indexes = null)`: Averages triangle normals across index triples.
- `Normal(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Face face)`: Evaluates face normal. If face has `<= 6` indices (triangles/quads), returns `Normal(p0, p1, p2)`. If face has `> 6` indices (n-gons), calculates the best fitting plane normal using `Projection.FindBestPlane(positions, face.distinctIndexesInternal).normal`, ensuring positive alignment with the first triangle normal via `Vector3.Dot(nrm, prj)`.
- `NormalTangentBitangent(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Face face)`: Derives orthonormal surface basis from vertex positions and UV coordinates:
  a. Extracts positions `v1, v2, v3` and UV coordinates `w1, w2, w3` for the first triangle.
  b. Computes spatial vectors `x1 = v2.x - v1.x`, `y1 = v2.y - v1.y`, `z1 = v2.z - v1.z`, `x2 = v3.x - v1.x`, `y2 = v3.y - v1.y`, `z2 = v3.z - v1.z`, and UV deltas `s1 = w2.x - w1.x`, `s2 = w3.x - w1.x`, `t1 = w2.y - w1.y`, `t2 = w3.y - w1.y`.
  c. Calculates reciprocal determinant `r = 1.0f / (s1 * t2 - s2 * t1)` and derives surface tangents:
     $$sdir = \frac{(t_2 \Delta v_1 - t_1 \Delta v_2)}{s_1 t_2 - s_2 t_1}, \quad tdir = \frac{(s_1 \Delta v_2 - s_2 \Delta v_1)}{s_1 t_2 - s_2 t_1}$$
  d. Orthonormalizes tangent against normal with `Vector3.OrthoNormalize(ref n, ref tan1)`.
  e. Determines tangent handedness sign `tan.w = Dot(Cross(n, tan1), tan2) < 0f ? -1f : 1f`.
  f. Computes bitangent `bitangent = Cross(nrm, ((Vector3)tan) * tan.w)`.

7. Vector Helpers and Transform Utilities:
- Vector approximations: `Approx2`, `Approx3`, `Approx4`, `ApproxC`, `Approx` compare vector components against `delta = 0.0001f`.
- Component utilities: `Abs`, `Sign`, `Sum`, `DivideBy`, `IsCardinalAxis`, `MakeNonZero`, `FixNaN`, `EnsureUnitVector`.
- `TransformUtility.TransformVertex(this Transform transform, Vertex vertex)`: Converts vertex position via `transform.TransformPoint`, normal via `transform.TransformDirection`, and tangent via `transform.rotation * vertex.tangent`, preserving colors and UV channels 0 through 4.
- `TransformUtility.InverseTransformVertex(this Transform transform, Vertex vertex)`: Converts vertex position with `transform.InverseTransformPoint`, normal with `transform.InverseTransformDirection`, and tangent with `transform.InverseTransformDirection`.
sections.godot_notes: Godot 4's `Geometry3D` and `Geometry2D` provide built-in equivalents for segment-segment intersection (`Geometry2D.segment_intersects_segment`), ray-triangle intersection (`Geometry3D.ray_intersects_triangle`), and point-in-polygon (`Geometry2D.is_point_in_polygon`). The `Transform3D` class directly handles vertex transformations with `transform * position` (points) and `transform.basis * normal` (directions). Tangent and bitangent generation matches the standard MikkTSpace / Gram-Schmidt conventions used in Godot's `SurfaceTool.generate_tangents()`.

sections.heading: PROJECTION
sections.content:
The `Projection` static class provides 3D-to-2D projection, planar fitting, spherical mapping, and 2D contour polygon sorting methods. These functions are critical for UV unwrapping, Auto-UV texture projection, face triangulation, and polygon hole cutting.

1. Least-Squares Best Plane Fitting (`FindBestPlane`):
- `Projection.FindBestPlane(IList<Vector3> points, IList<int> indexes = null)`: Fits an optimal 3D plane through an arbitrary set of non-coplanar or coplanar points using covariance matrix analysis.
  a. Computes centroid `c` by averaging coordinates across all target vertices:
     $$c = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=0}^{N-1} p_i$$
  b. Computes centered second-moment sums (elements of the covariance matrix):
     $$xx = \sum (p_{ix} - c_x)^2, \quad yy = \sum (p_{iy} - c_y)^2, \quad zz = \sum (p_{iz} - c_z)^2$$
     $$xy = \sum (p_{ix} - c_x)(p_{iy} - c_y), \quad xz = \sum (p_{ix} - c_x)(p_{iz} - c_z), \quad yz = \sum (p_{iy} - c_y)(p_{iz} - c_z)$$
  c. Calculates the 2x2 minor determinants:
     $$det_x = yy \cdot zz - yz^2, \quad det_y = xx \cdot zz - xz^2, \quad det_z = xx \cdot yy - xy^2$$
  d. Selects the primary normal component based on the largest determinant:
     - If `det_x > det_y` and `det_x > det_z`: Sets $n_x = 1.0$, $n_y = \frac{xz \cdot yz - xy \cdot zz}{det_x}$, $n_z = \frac{xy \cdot yz - xz \cdot yy}{det_x}$.
     - Else if `det_y > det_z`: Sets $n_x = \frac{yz \cdot xz - xy \cdot zz}{det_y}$, $n_y = 1.0$, $n_z = \frac{xy \cdot xz - yz \cdot xx}{det_y}$.
     - Otherwise: Sets $n_x = \frac{yz \cdot xy - xz \cdot yy}{det_z}$, $n_y = \frac{xz \cdot xy - yz \cdot xx}{det_z}$, $n_z = 1.0$.
  e. Normalizes `n` and returns `new Plane(n, c)`.
- `Projection.FindBestPlane(ProBuilderMesh mesh, int textureGroup)`: Iterates across all faces matching `face.textureGroup == textureGroup`, accumulates vertices from their index buffers, and executes the identical covariance fitting algorithm to generate a shared projection plane for the entire texture group.

2. Planar Projection Algorithm (`PlanarProject`):
- `PlanarProject(IList<Vector3> positions, IList<int> indexes, Vector3 direction, List<Vector2> results)`:
  a. Ensures unit normal vector `nrm = Math.EnsureUnitVector(direction)`.
  b. Maps `nrm` to dominant axis enum `axis = VectorToProjectionAxis(nrm)`.
  c. Retrieves projection tangent vector `prj = GetTangentToAxis(axis)`:
     - `ProjectionAxis.X` / `ProjectionAxis.XNegative`: returns `Vector3.up`.
     - `ProjectionAxis.Y` / `ProjectionAxis.YNegative`: returns `Vector3.forward`.
     - `ProjectionAxis.Z` / `ProjectionAxis.ZNegative`: returns `Vector3.up`.
  d. Computes orthonormal 2D projection axes:
     $$u = (nrm \times prj).\text{normalized}, \quad v = (u \times nrm).\text{normalized}$$
  e. Projects each 3D point `p` into 2D UV coordinates using dot products:
     $$uv.x = u \cdot p, \quad uv.y = v \cdot p$$
- `PlanarProject(ProBuilderMesh mesh, Face face, Vector3 projection = default)`: Projects face vertices to `mesh.texturesInternal`. If `face.uv.useWorldSpace` is enabled, vertex positions are transformed using `mesh.transform.TransformPoint` and normals with `mesh.transform.TransformDirection` prior to projection.
- `PlanarProject(ProBuilderMesh mesh, int textureGroup, AutoUnwrapSettings unwrapSettings)`: Computes an average normal across all faces in the texture group, optionally transforms it to world space, and projects texture group vertices uniformly into UV space.

3. Spherical Projection and Contour Sorting:
- `SphericalProject(IList<Vector3> vertices, IList<int> indexes = null)`: Computes centroid `cen = Math.Average(vertices, indexes)`. For each vertex, computes normalized vector `p = (v - cen).normalized`, generating equirectangular UVs:
  $$uv.x = 0.5 + \frac{\text{atan2}(p.z, p.x)}{2\pi}, \quad uv.y = 0.5 - \frac{\text{asin}(p.y)}{\pi}$$
- `Projection.Sort(IList<Vector2> verts, SortMethod method = SortMethod.CounterClockwise)`: Sorts 2D points into a continuous polygon boundary. Computes 2D centroid `cen = Math.Average(verts)` and calculates `Math.SignedAngle(Vector2.up, verts[i] - cen)` for every vertex. Sorts vertices ascending by angle (or reverses the list for `SortMethod.Clockwise`).
- `VectorToProjectionAxis(Vector3 direction)`: Determines dominant projection axis (`X`, `XNegative`, `Y`, `YNegative`, `Z`, `ZNegative`) by comparing absolute values `|x|`, `|y|`, `|z|` with `Math.Approx` tie-breaking.
- `ProjectionAxisToVector(ProjectionAxis axis)`: Maps `ProjectionAxis` enum directly to `Vector3.right`, `Vector3.up`, `Vector3.forward`, `-Vector3.right`, `-Vector3.up`, or `-Vector3.forward`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, planar projection for Auto-UV unwrapping and polygon triangulation is performed by fitting a `Plane` to 3D surface vertices using least-squares covariance, constructing a `Basis` whose Z axis aligns with the plane normal, and transforming points into the basis plane where $(X, Y)$ become UV coordinates. Polygon contour winding sorting can be accomplished with `Geometry2D.is_polygon_clockwise()`.

sections.heading: HANDLE UTILITY
sections.content:
`HandleUtility` provides spatial raycasting, camera-to-GUI coordinate transformation, selection orientation calculations, and picking utilities for ProBuilder editor tools.

1. Screen and GUI Point Conversions:
- `ScreenToGuiPoint(this Camera camera, Vector3 point, float pixelsPerPoint)`: Converts a screen coordinate (`(0,0)` bottom-left in pixels) to a GUI coordinate (`(0,0)` top-left in points):
  $$\text{guiPoint} = \left( \frac{\text{point.x}}{\text{pixelsPerPoint}}, \frac{\text{camera.pixelHeight} - \text{point.y}}{\text{pixelsPerPoint}}, \text{point.z} \right)$$

2. Face Raycasting Algorithms (`FaceRaycast`):
- `FaceRaycast(Ray worldRay, ProBuilderMesh mesh, out RaycastHit hit, float distance, CullingMode cullingMode, HashSet<Face> ignore = null)`:
  a. Transforms `worldRay` into mesh model space:
     - `worldRay.origin -= mesh.transform.position`
     - `worldRay.origin = mesh.transform.worldToLocalMatrix * worldRay.origin`
     - `worldRay.direction = mesh.transform.worldToLocalMatrix * worldRay.direction`
  b. Iterates through all faces in `mesh.facesInternal` (skipping any face in `ignore`).
  c. For each face, iterates over triangle index triples `j, j+1, j+2`:
     - Retrieves triangle vertices `a = positions[indexes[j]]`, `b = positions[indexes[j+1]]`, `c = positions[indexes[j+2]]`.
     - Calculates face normal `nrm = Vector3.Cross(b - a, c - a)` and ray dot product `dot = Vector3.Dot(worldRay.direction, nrm)`.
     - Evaluates `cullingMode`:
       - `CullingMode.Front`: Skips if `dot < 0f` (front-facing triangle).
       - `CullingMode.Back`: Skips if `dot > 0f` (back-facing triangle).
       - `CullingMode.FrontBack`: Tests both sides.
     - Calls `Math.RayIntersectsTriangle(worldRay, a, b, c, out dist, out point)`.
     - If intersected and `dist < OutHitPoint` and `dist <= distance`, records `OutHitPoint = dist`, `OutHitFace = i`, and `OutNrm = nrm`.
  d. Returns `RaycastHit(OutHitPoint, worldRay.GetPoint(OutHitPoint), OutNrm, OutHitFace)`.
- `FaceRaycastBothCullModes`: In a single pass, tracks the nearest front-facing face and nearest back-facing face intersecting `worldRay`, returning results via two reference item pairs for front and back hit geometry.
- `FaceRaycast(Ray InWorldRay, ProBuilderMesh mesh, out List<RaycastHit> hits, CullingMode cullingMode, HashSet<Face> ignore = null)`: Returns all intersected faces sorted by occurrence.

3. Raw Mesh Raycasting and Occlusion:
- `MeshRaycast(Ray InWorldRay, GameObject gameObject, out RaycastHit hit, float distance = Mathf.Infinity)`: Raycasts against standard `MeshFilter.sharedMesh` geometry using model-space transformed ray `transform.InverseTransformRay(InWorldRay)` and invokes `MeshRaycast(ray, mesh.vertices, mesh.triangles, out hit, distance)`.
- `MeshRaycast(Ray InRay, Vector3[] mesh, int[] triangles, out RaycastHit hit, float distance)`: Iterates over triangles using non-allocating `Math.RayIntersectsTriangle2(o, d, a, b, c, ref distance, ref n)`, tracking the closest hit face index `hitFace = CurTri / 3`.
- `InverseTransformRay(this Transform transform, Ray InWorldRay)`: Converts a world ray to local coordinates:
  $$\text{origin} = \text{worldToLocalMatrix} * (\text{InWorldRay.origin} - \text{position}), \quad \text{direction} = \text{worldToLocalMatrix.MultiplyVector}(\text{InWorldRay.direction})$$
- `PointIsOccluded(Camera cam, ProBuilderMesh pb, Vector3 worldPoint)`: Constructs a ray from `worldPoint + dir * 0.0001f` towards camera position `cam.transform.position`. Executes `FaceRaycast` with `CullingMode.Front`; returns true if an intervening triangle occludes the point.

4. Handle and Gizmo Orientation Calculations:
- `GetRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<int> indices)`: Calculates gizmo rotation from vertex normals and tangents:
  a. Ensures normals and tangents are computed via `Normals.CalculateNormals(mesh)` and `Normals.CalculateTangents(mesh)`.
  b. Averages vertex normals `nrm` and tangents `tan` across all selected vertex indices.
  c. Computes bitangent `bit = Vector3.Cross(nrm, tan * tan.w)`.
  d. Returns `mesh.transform.rotation * Quaternion.LookRotation(nrm, bit)`.
- `GetFaceRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, HandleOrientation orientation, IEnumerable<Face> faces)`:
  - `HandleOrientation.ActiveElement`: Evaluates `GetFaceRotation(mesh, faces.Last())` using `Math.NormalTangentBitangent(mesh, face)` and returns `mesh.transform.rotation * Quaternion.LookRotation(nrm.normal, nrm.bitangent)`.
  - `HandleOrientation.ActiveObject`: Returns `mesh.transform.rotation`.
  - Default: Returns `Quaternion.identity` (World orientation).
- `GetEdgeRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, HandleOrientation orientation, IEnumerable<Edge> edges)`: Computes rotation for `edges.Last()` by looking up its associated face with `EdgeUtility.GetFace(mesh, edge)`.
- `GetVertexRotation(ProBuilderMesh mesh, HandleOrientation orientation, IEnumerable<int> vertices)`: Invokes `GetRotation(mesh, vertices)` for `ActiveElement` orientation.
- `GetActiveElementPosition(ProBuilderMesh mesh, IEnumerable<Face>/<Edge>/<int>)`: Computes world-space centroid `mesh.transform.TransformPoint(Math.GetBounds(mesh.positionsInternal, indexes).center)`.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, editor picking and gizmo interaction are handled in `EditorNode3DGizmo` and `EditorPlugin._forward_3d_gui_input()`. Camera ray generation uses `Camera3D.project_ray_origin(mouse_pos)` and `Camera3D.project_ray_normal(mouse_pos)`. Coordinate conversions between screen/viewport points and 3D rays are provided by `Camera3D.unproject_position()` and `Camera3D.project_position()`. Element orientation transforms use `Transform3D.looking_at(target, up)`.

sections.heading: BOUNDS 2D
sections.content:
`Bounds2D` is an axis-aligned 2D bounding box data structure designed for 2D spatial queries, UV unwrapping, UV editor layout, polygon containment tests, and screen-space element selection.

1. Data Structure and Properties:
- `center` (`Vector2`): The 2D midpoint of the bounding box, initialized to `Vector2.zero`.
- `m_Size` (`Vector2`): The width and height dimensions of the bounding box.
- `m_Extents` (`Vector2`): Half-size extents along X and Y axes (`m_Size * 0.5f`).
- `size` property getter/setter: Updating `size` automatically recalculates `m_Extents.x = m_Size.x * 0.5f` and `m_Extents.y = m_Size.y * 0.5f`.
- `extents` property: Read-only access to `m_Extents`.
- `corners` property: Returns a 4-element `Vector2[]` array containing the bounding box corners ordered top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right:
  - Corner 0: `new Vector2(center.x - extents.x, center.y + extents.y)`
  - Corner 1: `new Vector2(center.x + extents.x, center.y + extents.y)`
  - Corner 2: `new Vector2(center.x - extents.x, center.y - extents.y)`
  - Corner 3: `new Vector2(center.x + extents.x, center.y - extents.y)`

2. Constructors and Encapsulation:
- `Bounds2D()`: Default constructor initializing center and size to zero.
- `Bounds2D(Vector2 center, Vector2 size)`: Explicit initialization of center and size.
- `Bounds2D(IList<Vector2> points)`: Automatically invokes `SetWithPoints(points)` to compute bounds encapsulating all points.
- `Bounds2D(IList<Vector2> points, IList<int> indexes)`: Invokes `SetWithPoints(points, indexes)` to encapsulate the subset of points referenced by `indexes`.
- `Bounds2D(Vector3[] points, Edge[] edges)`: Extracts 2D $(X, Y)$ components from 3D points referenced by an array of `Edge` structs, computing `xMin`, `xMax`, `yMin`, `yMax` across edge vertices `.a` and `.b`.
- `Bounds2D(Vector2[] points, int length)`: Computes bounding rectangle across array elements up to `length`.
- `SetWithPoints(IList<Vector2> points)` / `SetWithPoints(IList<Vector2> points, IList<int> indexes)`: Iterates through coordinate list tracking `xMin`, `xMax`, `yMin`, `yMax`, then calculates:
  $$\text{center.x} = \frac{xMin + xMax}{2}, \quad \text{center.y} = \frac{yMin + yMax}{2}$$
  $$\text{m\_Size.x} = xMax - xMin, \quad \text{m\_Size.y} = yMax - yMin$$
  $$\text{m\_Extents.x} = \text{m\_Size.x} \cdot 0.5, \quad \text{m\_Extents.y} = \text{m\_Size.y} \cdot 0.5$$

3. Spatial Intersection and Containment Queries:
- `ContainsPoint(Vector2 point)`: Tests whether a 2D point lies within the bounding box bounds:
  $$\text{Inside} = !(point.x > center.x + extents.x \;\lor\; point.x < center.x - extents.x \;\lor\; point.y > center.y + extents.y \;\lor\; point.y < center.y - extents.y)$$
- `IntersectsLineSegment(Vector2 lineStart, Vector2 lineEnd)`: Evaluates if any portion of a 2D line segment intersects or lies within the bounding box:
  a. If `ContainsPoint(lineStart)` or `ContainsPoint(lineEnd)` is true, returns `true`.
  b. Otherwise, queries segment intersection against the four boundary edges formed by `corners` (`[0]-[1]`, `[1]-[3]`, `[3]-[2]`, `[2]-[0]`) using `Math.GetLineSegmentIntersect`.
- `Intersects(Bounds2D bounds)`: Separating Axis Test between two `Bounds2D` instances:
  $$\text{Overlap} = |\text{this.center.x} - \text{bounds.center.x}| \cdot 2 < (\text{this.size.x} + \text{bounds.size.x}) \;\land\; |\text{this.center.y} - \text{bounds.center.y}| \cdot 2 < (\text{this.size.y} + \text{bounds.size.y})$$
- `Intersects(Rect rect)`: Overlap test against a Unity `Rect` using the identical separating axis formulation.

4. Static Aggregation Utilities:
- `Bounds2D.Center(IList<Vector2> points)` / `Bounds2D.Center(IList<Vector2> points, IList<int> indexes)`: Computes the geometric center `(xMin + xMax) / 2, (yMin + yMax) / 2` without instantiating a `Bounds2D` object.
- `Bounds2D.Size(IList<Vector2> points, IList<int> indexes)`: Computes the bounding size `new Vector2(xMax - xMin, yMax - yMin)`.
- `Bounds2D.Center(IList<Vector4> points, IEnumerable<int> indexes)`: Extracts $(X, Y)$ components from 4D vectors (such as UV3/UV4 arrays) and returns their 2D bounding center.
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, `Rect2` directly provides 2D axis-aligned bounding box functionality with `Rect2.position`, `Rect2.size`, `Rect2.end`, `Rect2.has_point()`, `Rect2.intersects()`, and `Rect2.encloses()`. `Rect2.grow()` and `Rect2.merge()` can encapsulate multiple 2D points.

sections.heading: INT VECTORS
sections.content:
The `IntVec2`, `IntVec3`, and `IntVec4` structs along with the `VectorHash` static utility provide integer-quantized vector representation and fuzzy hashing.

1. Purpose and Design Rationale:
- In geometric modeling and mesh manipulation, spatial algorithms (transformations, extrusions, rotations, planar projections) subject vertex coordinates to floating-point drift. Two vertices that are geometrically coincident may differ by negligible precision noise (for example, `0.00700000001f` versus `0.00700000000f`).
- Standard floating-point equality (`operator==`) and default `GetHashCode` implementations fail to match these coincident coordinates, causing vertex welding, shared vertex table generation (`SharedVertex`), seam calculation, and winged-edge topology building to create redundant or disconnected vertices.
- `IntVec` solves this by scaling floating-point components by a fixed resolution multiplier `VectorHash.FltCompareResolution = 1000f` and quantizing them to integer values using `System.Convert.ToInt32(v * 1000f)`. This establishes an automatic tolerance threshold of $0.001$ ($1 / 1000$), grouping all vertices within that epsilon into identical integer buckets.

2. Structure and Properties:
- `IntVec2`: Implements `IEquatable<IntVec2>`. Contains `public Vector2 value`, read-only accessors `x => value.x`, `y => value.y`, and constructor `IntVec2(Vector2 vector)`.
- `IntVec3`: Implements `IEquatable<IntVec3>`. Contains `public Vector3 value`, read-only accessors `x => value.x`, `y => value.y`, `z => value.z`, and constructor `IntVec3(Vector3 vector)`.
- `IntVec4`: Implements `IEquatable<IntVec4>`. Contains `public Vector4 value`, read-only accessors `x => value.x`, `y => value.y`, `z => value.z`, `w => value.w`, and constructor `IntVec4(Vector4 vector)`.

3. Quantization and Equality Operations:
- Quantization method:
  `private static int round(float v) => System.Convert.ToInt32(v * VectorHash.FltCompareResolution);`
- `Equals(IntVec3 p)` / `Equals(Vector3 p)`: Compares quantized integer coordinates across all axes:
  `round(x) == round(p.x) && round(y) == round(p.y) && round(z) == round(p.z)`
- `operator==` and `operator!=`: Delegate directly to `a.Equals(b)`.
- `Equals(object b)`: Supports comparisons against both `IntVecN` and raw `VectorN` instances.
- Zero-cost implicit conversions:
  - `public static implicit operator Vector3(IntVec3 p) => p.value;`
  - `public static implicit operator IntVec3(Vector3 p) => new IntVec3(p);`
  (Identical bidirectional implicit conversions exist for `IntVec2` <-> `Vector2` and `IntVec4` <-> `Vector4`).

4. Fuzzy Hashing Utility (`VectorHash`):
- `VectorHash` provides high-performance hash code generation directly from floating-point vectors without requiring `IntVec` struct instantiation or heap allocations.
- Constant: `public const float FltCompareResolution = 1000f;`
- Quantized float hash function:
  `static int HashFloat(float f) { ulong u = (ulong)(f * FltCompareResolution); return (int)(u % int.MaxValue); }`
- Hash combination algorithm: Employs a polynomial rolling hash initialized with prime seed `27` and multiplied by prime `29` within an `unchecked` block:
  - `GetHashCode(Vector2 v)`:
    `int hash = 27; hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.x); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.y); return hash;`
  - `GetHashCode(Vector3 v)`:
    `int hash = 27; hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.x); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.y); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.z); return hash;`
  - `GetHashCode(Vector4 v)`:
    `int hash = 27; hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.x); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.y); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.z); hash = hash * 29 + HashFloat(v.w); return hash;`
sections.godot_notes: In Godot 4, `Vector3i` and `Vector2i` provide integer vector types. To implement spatial quantization for shared vertex tables in Godot, coordinates can be converted using `Vector3i((v * 1000.0).round())` or `Vector3.snapped(Vector3(0.001, 0.001, 0.001))`. In GDScript / C#, `Vector3i` implements built-in hashing and equality comparison, allowing direct use as `Dictionary` or `HashSet` keys.

cross_references.relationship: ProBuilderMesh core data model stores vertex positions, faces, and shared vertex tables indexed and transformed by Math and ProBuilderSnapping
Face, Edge, and Vertex structures whose normals, tangents, areas, and bounds are calculated using Math and Projection
MeshArrays, RefreshMask, and NormalTangentBitangent calculations supporting vertex attribute generation
Auto-UV projection, texture group alignment, and planar unwrapping rely on Projection.PlanarProject and Projection.FindBestPlane
UV Editor canvas transformations, grid snapping, and UV bounding box queries utilize Bounds2D and ProBuilderSnapping
Scene view element picking and occlusion queries rely on HandleUtility.FaceRaycast and PointIsOccluded
Translation, rotation, and scale tools execute grid snapping and handle orientation via EditorSnapping and HandleUtility
Winged-edge mesh topology construction and vertex coincidence grouping depend on IntVec3 and VectorHash
